title: Fitted moment slopes gave no clear centroid-delay prediction gain for selected GCMT events in 2012-2020
abstract: We tested whether fitted moment slopes improve positive centroid-delay estimates over a fixed exponent of 1/3. We used selected GCMT events with Mw 6.5 to below 7.5 and centroid depths below 70 km or at least 300 km. Each test year in 2012-2020 used only earlier records from 2004 onward for fitting. Separate depth slopes gave an equal-depth mean relative log MSE reduction of -1.10%. The conditional 95% two-year block interval was -5.50% to +1.48%. The test had 228 shallow and 33 deep events. Thus the fitted slopes gave no clear gain. A full-sample fit gave a common exponent of 0.237, which shows why a fitted slope alone is not prediction evidence. A short test, few deep events, revised records and catalog errors limit the result. The package gives code, source hashes, score aggregates, an independent numerical audit and a figure. External event records are not bundled.

display.caption: Later-year log delay errors and equal-depth gains. Intervals use paired two-year blocks of test years, conditional on the fitted models. Centroid delay is not full rupture duration.

citations.reason: We reuse its documented external source snapshot and parser design. We test the scaling assumption in a chronological score on overlapping data.
Its catalog-era audit motivates use of 2004-2020.
